html:
The Beheading of Saint John the Baptist is a large painting that Caravaggio made in 1608 for the Knights of Malta. It hangs in the Co-Cathedral of St John in Valletta.

Caravaggio had fled Rome after killing a man in a fight. In Malta he was made a knight of the Hospitaller order and painted this scene for its oratory. It shows the moment just after the blow, in a dim prison courtyard, with a few figures and a great deal of dark space. It is the only work he signed, in the blood flowing from the saint's neck.

Within months he was jailed after a brawl, escaped, and was expelled from the order. The painting is the most famous work of art in Malta.
sum: The Beheading of Saint John the Baptist is a large painting that Caravaggio made in 1608 for the Knights of Malta. It hangs in the Co-Cathedral of St John in Valletta.
